transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad for a really long time now. On top of that, I keep hearing voices and seeing things that other people can't see.
Do the voices or visions ever happen when you are not feeling depressed, or do they only occur during times when your depression is at its worst?

They actually happen during both times. There have been periods, lasting for at least two weeks, where my mood was relatively normal but I was still hearing and seeing things. But they definitely happen when I'm feeling deeply depressed as well.
Over the whole time you’ve been ill, have the depressive episodes been present for most of the illness, or have the voices and visions happened mostly outside of depression?

The depression has definitely been there for the vast majority of the time I've been unwell. But there was a period of about two or three weeks where my mood felt completely normal, even though the voices and visions were still happening.
Since these symptoms started, have they caused a major drop in how you function at work, school, or in relationships?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't thought much about how it has impacted my overall functioning lately.
During the times you felt depressed, did you also have other depression symptoms like loss of interest, low energy, guilt, poor sleep, or appetite changes nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes, I've had almost no energy and feel completely exhausted, both physically and mentally, nearly every day for about seven months, along with a major change in my appetite. I haven't really felt guilty or noticed major sleep issues, but this lack of energy and appetite changes have been very persistent.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked faster than usual, or had racing thoughts?
No, I've never had any periods where I felt unusually energetic or euphoric like that. My energy has always been very low, and I've never experienced racing thoughts or felt on top of the world.
Thinking about the entire course of your illness, would you say the depression has been present for more than half of the total time since the voices and visions began?

Yes, definitely. The depression and low mood have been present for the vast majority of the time since the voices and visions first started. It feels like the sadness has been a constant weight for well over half of that entire time.
Even during the weeks when your mood felt normal, did you still have things like low motivation, reduced emotional expression, or social withdrawal?

Yes, even during those weeks, I had absolutely no motivation to do anything and barely wanted to talk to anyone. My family also told me that I seemed very flat, like I wasn't showing any real emotion in my face or voice. It felt like I was just completely shut off from the world.

During those two or three weeks when your mood felt normal but the voices and visions continued, were you truly free of depressed mood and loss of interest most days, or did some depression still linger in the background?

During those weeks, my mood was completely back to normal and I didn't feel depressed or lose interest in things at all. The sadness and emptiness were entirely gone during that brief period, even though I was still hearing the voices and seeing things.
Can you tell me whether the voices, visions, or the lack of motivation have made it hard for you to keep up with work, school, daily chores, or relationships compared with how you were before?

Yes, they have made things incredibly difficult. I have no motivation to do simple chores around the house or keep up with any daily activities, and I've completely stopped talking to my friends and family. It feels impossible to maintain any kind of routine or relationship anymore.

Schizophrenia remains in the differential because persistent psychosis with negative symptoms and impairment can fit, but it is less favored given the patient's report that depressive episodes have occupied most of the total illness duration. No evidence of mania was elicited, making bipolar-spectrum schizoaffective diagnoses less likely and not candidates here.

candidates: Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
inference_history.note: There were no previous candidates provided. Based on this initial conversation, the patient reports a long period of depressed mood plus auditory and visual hallucinations. This raises concern for a primary psychotic disorder such as Schizophrenia, a mood disorder with psychotic symptoms such as Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features, or Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) if psychosis occurs along with substantial depressive episodes and possibly outside mood episodes. Major Depressive Disorder without psychotic features remains a less likely placeholder only because the depressive syndrome is clearly present, but the hallucinations make a psychotic-spectrum or psychotic depression diagnosis more likely. More questioning is needed about the timing of psychotic symptoms relative to mood episodes, duration, functional decline, and other psychotic/manic symptoms.

There is no history of mania or hypomania. This pattern is most consistent with Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) rather than Schizophrenia.
